defects_found_on_device: D1 (d4b5f73): _registry and _director were `late final` and the refresh path reassigns both, so the first install with an avatar on screen threw LateInitializationError and drew a red error box over every companion. No test reached it: the refresh needs a rebuild, and no test installed under a mounted avatar. Two regression tests added; restoring `late final` fails both.

D2 (c0c92dc): the installed-pack registry was in memory only, so a cold start offered only the built-ins and silently discarded the persisted selection. Fixed with an install record at the pack root plus a directory scan; a pack neither source can classify is skipped and reported, never guessed.
D3 (a23d7ba): recovery read a hand-copied pack from its own manifest and kept nothing, so every launch re-hashed every frame and re-derived the name. Recovery now writes the records.
p32_gaps_closed: frame content: the validator judges names and never bytes, so nothing checked that a file called idle_000.png is a PNG. The importer now checks the PNG signature of every referenced frame before anything is written.
p32_claims_corrected: The reader's `unreadable_archive` branch is effectively unreachable. ZipDecoder in archive 4.3.0 does not throw for unparseable input - measured: garbage, half-truncated, and 8-byte-header inputs all return a zero-file archive, and corrupt bytes in the middle still yield files. Malformed input arrives as `empty_archive` or as a manifest validation failure. Safety is unchanged (refused, zero files) but the old comment described an unreachable path.
open_findings: CORRECTED at b13e7b1: productionise.measure and asset_pipeline.measure read split()[-1] as alpha, which is the palette index on an indexed PNG - but BOTH call sites already convert to RGBA first, so nothing was broken. The earlier note called it a bug; checking it properly says it was a latent trap. Both functions now convert for themselves and refuse an empty frame, proven by tools/test_measure_alpha.py against 147 real indexed frames (115 of which distinguish the two channels, so the proof is not vacuous).
P32: symlink rejection is NOT verified through the reader, and duplicate-name ZIP entries cannot be built with ZipEncoder. Both rules are covered directly at the policy level only.
P32: the expansion-ratio bomb check is inert on this path; per-entry and total byte caps still apply.
P32: recovery reads every frame of a pack that has no record, to compute its digest. Fine for one pack; revisit if many are dropped in by hand.

process_notes: Never write file content through a shell heredoc in this environment: it has silently truncated content three times. Use the file tool and verify after writing.
Prefer patching by rewriting a file whole over matching long anchors: dart format rewraps and breaks anchors silently.

The screen is not evidence for state. Verify against the device filesystem, the database, or an instrumented trace. The device SQLite holds its rows in the -wal file: pull the .sqlite, -wal and -shm together or the tables read as empty.
The emulator window can be minimised, and a minimised window reports bounds at -32000. Clicks then go nowhere with no error; getScreenshot restores it on Windows.

Neither tap method is universal: adb input tap at scaled device coordinates reached the install button CUA missed, and CUA reached the import bar and the ... menu that adb taps missed. Try the other before concluding a control is broken.
The device screen is 1080x2400 and the CUA raster 561x1280, so the scale is about 1.925.

A soft keyboard covers the bottom of the screen and eats taps meant for a button below the field. Dismiss it at the Android level (input keyevent 4) rather than by tapping, which can land in the field and type.
After the file picker has been used, am start resolves to it. force-stop the app and launch with monkey -p <pkg> -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1.

A provider that is only `read` in a test is not invalidated when its dependency changes. Subscribe with `container.listen` before triggering the change, or the assertion is against a value that never recomputes. This cost two rounds here and produced a false finding.

The cupertino_icons font warning during a release build is not ours: lib/ references no CupertinoIcons and pubspec does not declare the package, so it is a transitive tree-shaking artifact and no glyphs are missing.

Damaged-pack hardening: 8 tests covering a manifest corrupted while running, missing frames, a deleted pack directory, availability for a damaged pack, and a cold start over a damaged root. The picker does not offer a pack it cannot read, and the app is never left unable to name the selected companion.

RESOLVED, and withdrawn as a finding: the earlier note said an already-alive companionCatalogProvider did not recompute after a pack became unreadable. It does. A traced diagnostic shows two emits - [dog,cat,rabbit,mimi] then [dog,cat,rabbit,other] - so the damaged pack stops being offered without a restart. The earlier observation was an artifact of reading the provider without a listener first: a provider that is only `read` is not invalidated when its dependency changes, which is a fact about `read`, not about the catalog. The test now subscribes the way a widget does and asserts the recomputation, and passes deterministically across runs.

Accessibility on the import screen: 4 tests. The file button, the three species chips and the install button are all reachable by semantics, a chosen species announces as selected, and the completeness report is present as text rather than only as an amber pill. Reduced motion is honoured for a custom companion by construction - the same director and the same context, with no per-companion branch - which custom_companion_first_class_test already asserts.

Sprite-cache bound: CompanionPackValidator.maxFramesPerAction = 64. The player precaches the active sequence in full, deliberately, so an action declaring thousands of frames was a pack that exhausts memory by being well formed - the archive policy allows 4096 entries and a decoded 512x512 RGBA frame is about a megabyte. Refused at import rather than trimmed, and the refusal names the bound. Two tests: over the bound is refused, at the bound is accepted.

Process death mid-session was already covered and needed no new work: persistence_recovery_test covers an active session, a pause, and a session while finishing, and golden_flow_test covers the abandoned finishing session a kill leaves behind, settling it exactly once.
p39_remaining: A device pass over the accessibility work: the assertions are widget-level and a TalkBack pass would be the real check, which needs a person listening.
